name: Google Earth Basemap
author: NakshaTech
description:
Universal VTK-native basemap plugin for NakshaAI. Two free, no-key providers are built in - Esri World Imagery (satellite) and OpenStreetMap (street/roadmap) - matching the reference Urban Surve platform project. Google Satellite/Roadmap/Terrain remain optional when the user provides a Google Maps Platform API key. Basemap tiles auto-refresh on every camera pan/zoom (including programmatic zoom performed by the host app).
- External ZIP install with no core app edits
- Esri World Imagery satellite works without an API key
- OpenStreetMap street/roadmap works without an API key
- Auto-refresh tiles on zoom in/out and pan (camera ModifiedEvent observer)
- Optional official Google Map Tiles API support
- 2D Top/Plan View integration
- Project CRS reprojection with pyproj, reading the host's authoritative canvas CRS (gui.crs_manager) when available
- 1.1.7: removed the EPSG:3857 fallback used while real project data has an unresolved CRS (tiles now refuse to render misaligned rather than guessing); added on_canvas_crs_changed() so the host's canvas-CRS notification reaches this plugin directly; past a location's real Esri imagery resolution, the deepest available tile now stays on screen (stretched) instead of showing Esri's own "Map data not yet available" placeholder graphic
- 1.1.8: tiles now load center-out instead of scanline order so the view fills in steadily instead of popping in at random spots; Esri requests are split across its two mirror hostnames for roughly double effective download concurrency
- 1.1.14: ribbon UI kept as the original QFrame panel + plain-text Basemap/Refresh/Go To/Settings buttons (no icons, no RibbonSection) - a v1.1.9/1.1.10 attempt at icon-based styling stretched the ribbon bar and was reverted; runs on the v1.1.8 backend (center-out tile loading, Esri mirror-host concurrency, overzoom placeholder rejection, CRS hooks); provider dropdown labels cleaned to "Esri World Imagery (Free)" / "OpenStreetMap (Free)" / "Google Satellite" / "Google Roadmap" / "Google Terrain" (no "API key" wording)
- 1.1.16: SNT-first priority rule (SNT CRS overrides canvas CRS; detaching SNT restores point cloud CRS); resilient DGN SpatialRef and multi-PRJ fallback resolution; Canadian and polar domain bounds protection
- Async Qt network requests with free-provider host fallback
- VTK-native JPEG/PNG tile decoding
- Provider attribution
- Clean enable/disable/reinstall/uninstall lifecycle
- 1.1.17: Extreme zoom-out full canvas coverage & amoeba elimination (world-extent coordinate clamping for Web Mercator; robust sample-grid projection bounding; out-of-domain singularity tile rejection)
- 1.1.18: Fixed SNT/DXF/GIS data occasionally rendering behind the basemap - the Z-separation used to keep the basemap under real data was a fixed tiny epsilon that depth-buffer precision could swallow at real-world coordinate magnitudes; now scales with camera view distance like the existing placeholder-tile separation
- 1.1.20: fixed tiles never finishing to load on wide / zoomed-out views. Two compounding bugs in the fetch pipeline: _refresh_now() aborted EVERY in-flight tile download at the start of each debounced refresh, and _on_tile_finished() dropped any reply whose generation tag was not the newest - so a valid, still-needed tile was thrown away whenever a camera nudge or scroll settle ticked the generation mid-download. Zoomed in (few tiles) usually finished inside one 300ms window and looked fine; zoomed out (up to 36 tiles) took longer, so it was almost always killed and restarted, looping forever. Staleness is now decided by "is this tile still in the current view" (_active_ids membership) via the new _abort_unwanted_tile_replies() helper, so wanted tiles keep downloading across refreshes instead of restarting from zero
- 1.1.19: basemap tiles are routed through the host render pipeline (gui.scene_render_pipeline) so they stay on the raster layer beneath LiDAR/vector data; calls are now guarded with a fallback to the plain renderer, so the plugin still installs and runs on older app builds without that module
- 1.1.25: QGIS/ArcGIS-inspired projected-basemap stability pass. Non-Web-Mercator free basemaps are clipped to the official CRS area-of-use before reprojection; screen LOD is based on the clipped footprint instead of the full canvas; the old sparse 9x9 inverse-bounds sampler that collapsed EPSG:3301 to a single point at extreme zoom-out is replaced by dense domain-clipped sampling; OSM now uses the same flat inverse-resampled viewport path as Esri instead of forward-projected curved tile meshes; invalid projected pixels are transparent; stale basemap actors are cleared when the camera leaves the CRS domain; projected texture work is capped to 1024 px on the longest edge; OSM uses the policy-required tile.openstreetmap.org hostname; User-Agent updated to 1.1.26. Correction: 1.1.25 did run this on a QThreadPool as described above, but 1.1.26 (this file's prior release) reverted it back onto the Qt GUI thread - a background-thread pass could access-violate inside proj_9-*.dll on Windows when it overlapped host CRS work during a GIS import (see README 'v1.1.26 - Windows PROJ crash fix'). README was updated for that revert at the time; this changelog line was not, and kept claiming QThreadPool through 1.1.26. Fixed here; see 1.1.27 below.
- 1.1.27: fixed two projected-basemap symptoms reported after 1.1.26. (1) "Shows nothing, then a small/wrong patch, and it keeps happening on every zoom-out": the composed viewport texture only ever replaced the one on screen once coverage reached 98.5%, and on a cold start (right after activate(), or right after any reset) there was no prior texture for that rule to "keep" - so the canvas showed nothing until coverage crossed that bar, and during continuous zooming a new view could keep missing the bar indefinitely while the previous, now-stale texture sat at its old world-space size and simply looked smaller (or larger) as the live camera kept moving. Fixed by (a) clearing the on-screen viewport actor immediately once the live camera scale has diverged from the scale it was composed for by more than 1.6x, instead of leaving it in place indefinitely, and (b) accepting a much lower first-paint coverage bar (20%) whenever there is no current viewport actor to keep, so a correct (if partial) image appears quickly and later compose passes still refine it up to the original 98.5% bar. (2) Compose debounce widened 55ms -> 90ms to reduce how often the synchronous NumPy/PROJ pass (see the correction note on 1.1.25 above) runs back-to-back during a burst of tile arrivals.
